The actual published definition gives only a measurable sample space, parameter labels, and a family of laws; it adds no measurability on parameter labels and no common probability space.
The actual published definition requires a real inner-product space complete in its induced norm.
The actual published definition identifies random elements as measurable maps into a measurable space; the item defines its cylinder sample through its coordinate maps.
The actual published definition states that L2(P) consists of almost-sure equivalence classes, matching the process linearity convention.
The actual published definition uses independence of the sigma-algebras generated by random elements; the isonormal finite-coordinate condition states mutual independence.
The actual published proof verifies the pushforward law is a probability measure by measurable preimages, total mass one, and countable additivity.

The actual published definition states that a Hilbert basis is a complete orthonormal family whose closed finite span is all of H; no enumeration is part of that definition, so this theorem supplies one explicitly.
The actual published proof establishes |<v,w>|<=||v||||w|| for real or complex inner-product spaces. Its hypotheses hold for H and are used only to bound the deterministic mean tail.
The actual published definition gives the logarithmic coefficient norm, states the trace threshold, and proves the coefficient map L2([0,1])->H(delta) is continuous.

The actual published proof uses countable choice and proves the specified independent density-normal coefficient sequence is Borel Gaussian in H(delta) exactly for delta>1/2, and is not L2-valued in infinite dimension.

The actual published definition states AC_omega; it is assumed only for the H(delta) Borel-carrier clause through the white-noise lemma. The coordinate-law and mean-square expansion arguments do not use it.
